answer:
Loom has no auto-scaling GPU cluster mode. I found nothing about it in the docs or the feature list, so there's no switch to turn on, and I won't invent one.

Loom doesn't manage hardware at all. Each agent names a model with `model:`, and that model runs wherever its provider runs it. Your three agents (Researcher, Writer, Editor) all use `gemini-2.5-flash`, so Google handles the scaling. The docs also describe a `routing` policy with `strategy: fallback` or `cost_aware`, which picks between models by cost or falls back when one fails.

If you want to host the model yourself, a local Ollama model is a free option for the first real runs. If you want GPU-backed inference, you'd run that serving layer outside Loom and point an agent at it.

Are you after lower cost, more throughput, or running on your own hardware? The answer decides whether model routing or a local model fits.
